mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the median return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND HOUST MoM change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during these episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 0.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) while payroll employment (PAYEMS) is flat or falling signals a supply-side contraction, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM change < -0.5% AND PAYEMS MoM change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% within a single month signals an emergency easing response to a financial shock, which historically coincides with a positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days due to risk-on sentiment and liquidity effects.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of more than 1% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a demand expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 MoM change > 1% AND HOUST MoM change > 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months, accompanied by a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below the inflation rate, signals a failure of monetary policy to contain inflation, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to heightened uncertainty and real rate concerns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for six consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < CPIAUCSL for all six months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
